correctness.rationale: An elementary cubic triangle-free first-force argument proves Z>=4; a row-occupancy case split (4+0,3+1,2+2) exhausts every four-set that can start and continue forcing. Each of the five resulting explicit templates is shown to force the full graph. A finite integer-offset comparison of templates establishes a uniform five-by-five exchange-neighbor table for n>=6, with n=6,7 boundary identifications checked separately. The handshake identity yields 48n edges and the table gives the exact degree polynomial. Explicit C-align to C-shift exchange chains connect all types. An independent brute-force graph-forcing checker tests all three- and four-sets at n=5..13; a separately constructed symbolic-template checker validates counts, table and connectivity at n=6..50. Outputs and hashes from actual package files were checked. Finite tests do not serve as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The known zero-forcing number four and the generic exchange-graph definition are not claimed. Full-text inspection of the 2011 prism zero-forcing source (its Cartesian-product theorem and index discussion), and of the 2020 minimum zero-forcing reconfiguration paper (its graph families and structural results), finds no statement entailing an all-n five-family enumeration, 13n state count, 48n connected exchange graph, or full degree enumerator. Actual semantic mathematical-record searches and targeted literature searches find related but non-covering graph families and invariants. These checks support best-knowledge originality, not independent publication-priority certification.

value.rationale: The known minimal cardinality four does not determine the number or geometry of optimal blue seed sets. The theorem classifies every minimum initial state, detects five intrinsic row/offset types, determines exact local one-token mobility and global reachability for an infinite, symmetric, cubic graph family. The natural minimum-set exchange construction motivated the count and five-type degree profile; these are not a routine recalculation of Z=4. It does not infer shortest paths or mixing.
